provenance.sourceName: Hat Yai City Municipality — community boundary announcements (zones 1-4, Nov 2022 - May 2023) and 103-community map (rev. 2022-11-14)
provenance.geographicScope: เขต 1 (Zone 1) — communities listed in the zone announcement
provenance.methodology: Sum of the populations printed for 27 of 28 communities in the community-boundary announcement of เขต 1.
limitations: Announcement figures, not DOPA registration counts; reference date not stated; some communities missing or malformed.
DOPA registered population of the whole municipality is 138,582 at 2025-12-31; zone sums total 138,046 (different source and date).

provenance.sourceName: Approximate demonstration partition of Hat Yai municipality into zones 1-4 (derived)
provenance.methodology: Geodesic area of the published polygon (turf.area, WGS84), rounded to 0.001 km².
limitations: The polygon is an APPROXIMATE demonstration partition, not an official boundary; its area is indicative only.

provenance.sourceName: Derived: Hat Yai City Municipality — community boundary announcements (zones 1-4, Nov 2022 - May 2023) and 103-community map (rev. 2022-11-14) ÷ polygon area
provenance.methodology: population (33,852) ÷ areaKm2 (4.954 km²), rounded to 0.1 persons/km².
limitations: Announcement figures, not DOPA registration counts; reference date not stated; some communities missing or malformed.
DOPA registered population of the whole municipality is 138,582 at 2025-12-31; zone sums total 138,046 (different source and date).
Area comes from an approximate demonstration polygon.

provenance.sourceName: Allocated from Songkhla LAO survey (songkhla-gdcatalog-lao-waste) by zone population share
provenance.methodology: Municipality generated waste (ที่เกิดขึ้น) FY BE 2565 (276.72 t/day, Songkhla LAO survey) allocated to the 4 zones in proportion to zone population (sums of community figures printed in the 2022–2023 boundary announcements; total 138,046), with largest-remainder rounding to 0.01 t/day so the zones sum exactly to the municipality total.
limitations: ESTIMATED by allocation — no zone-level waste data is published; differences between zones only mirror population shares.
Zone polygons are an approximate demonstration partition.

provenance.sourceName: Allocated from Songkhla LAO survey (songkhla-gdcatalog-lao-waste) by zone population share
provenance.methodology: Municipality collected waste (เก็บขนได้) FY BE 2565 (184.09 t/day, Songkhla LAO survey) allocated to the 4 zones in proportion to zone population (sums of community figures printed in the 2022–2023 boundary announcements; total 138,046), with largest-remainder rounding to 0.01 t/day so the zones sum exactly to the municipality total.
limitations: ESTIMATED by allocation — no zone-level waste data is published; differences between zones only mirror population shares.
Zone polygons are an approximate demonstration partition.

provenance.sourceName: Urban Intelligence illustrative flood-risk / accumulation model v1.0.0
provenance.methodology: simulateAccumulation(inflow = wasteGenerated 67.86 t/day, η = 0.95 (baseline scenario), 30 daily steps, A₀ = 0) — final stock; steady state G·(1−η)/η = 3.57 t. Model v1.0.0; see docs/SIMULATION_MODEL.md §13.
limitations: Illustrative stock model, not a measured quantity of uncollected waste.

provenance.sourceName: Derived: allocated municipality collected waste ÷ zone population
provenance.methodology: Measure: COLLECTED waste (not generated). wasteCollected (45.14 t/day) × 1000 ÷ population (33,852). Zone waste is an allocation by population share.
limitations: Identical across zones by construction: zone waste is allocated by the same population figures it is divided by.
Cross-period: waste FY BE 2565 ÷ community figures printed in 2022–2023 announcements.
Uses collected waste only. A separate generated-waste figure (67.86 t/day (2022), status estimated) exists but is a different measure and is not mixed in.

provenance.sourceName: Derived: collected waste (Allocated from Songkhla LAO survey (songkhla-gdcatalog-lao-waste) by zone population share) ÷ polygon area
provenance.methodology: Measure: COLLECTED waste (not generated). wasteCollected (45.14 t/day) ÷ areaKm2 (4.954 km²).
limitations: Area comes from an approximate demonstration polygon.
Uses collected waste only. A separate generated-waste figure (67.86 t/day (2022), status estimated) exists but is a different measure and is not mixed in.

provenance.sourceName: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API — ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis (models=era5), daily and hourly precipitation
provenance.geographicScope: Area anchor of Zone 1 (IDW of 4 nearest ERA5 lattice points)
provenance.methodology: Mean of the annual totals of the area's IDW daily series (rain-areas.json) over complete calendar years: 2024 2,148.2 mm, 2025 2,320.7 mm.
limitations: ERA5 reanalysis cells are 0.25° (≈27–28 km): neighbouring areas mostly share the same cell(s), so rainfall differences between neighbouring areas are mostly NOT resolved — the IDW only smooths between cell values and adds no local detail.
Modelled reanalysis, not rain-gauge observations; ERA5 smooths convective storms.
For scale: the TMD 1991-2020 climatological normal at station 48569 (HAT YAI AIRPORT) is 1,756.0 mm/year (gauge statistic, different period and method).

provenance.sourceName: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API — ECMWF ERA5 reanalysis (models=era5), daily and hourly precipitation
provenance.geographicScope: Area anchor of Zone 1 (IDW of 4 nearest ERA5 lattice points)
provenance.methodology: Daily reanalysis total for the latest date in the series (2026-10-28, local day ≈ 23:00–23:00), from rain-areas.json (IDW of the ERA5 lattice).
limitations: ERA5 reanalysis cells are 0.25° (≈27–28 km): neighbouring areas mostly share the same cell(s), so rainfall differences between neighbouring areas are mostly NOT resolved — the IDW only smooths between cell values and adds no local detail.
Latest COMPLETE ERA5 day at retrieval (≈5-day latency) — not a real-time reading; preliminary ERA5T data may be revised. Real-time gauge snapshots are in stations.json.

provenance.sourceName: Urban Intelligence illustrative flood-risk / accumulation model v1.0.0
provenance.methodology: Modelled drainage stress (D × 100) from computeAreaRisk(model v1.0.0) with the BASELINE scenario (10 mm/h × 2 h, capacity reduction 0, obstruction 0.3, upstream 0.2, η 0.95), design intensity 60 mm/h, inputs E = 0.103, W = 0.585, rainSpatialFactor = 1 (area annual rainfall ÷ mean over the city's areas). See docs/SIMULATION_MODEL.md.
limitations: Illustrative scenario output — not an official flood forecast; weights and capacity are demo assumptions.

provenance.sourceName: Derived: OpenStreetMap waterways (osm-hy-waterways, osm-hy-water-areas)
provenance.methodology: E = 0.5 × share of zone area within 300 m of Khlong U-Taphao (OSM ways named คลองอู่ตะเภา / คลองอุ่ตะเภา) + 0.5 × share within 300 m of any mapped OSM waterway (lines and water-area polygons); 20 m sample lattice; shares are absolute (0–1), not min–max scaled, because there are only 4 zones. This zone: 0.0% and 20.5%.
limitations: Proxy index; no spatial flood-extent data for the November 2025 flood was available, so historical inundation is NOT included.
The Hat Yai flood, November 2025 (2025-11-19 – 2025-11-28) affected most of the municipality (see flood-events.json); this index does not reflect it spatially.
Computed on approximate zone polygons; OSM waterway completeness varies; relative within Hat Yai only.

provenance.sourceName: Derived: allocated collected waste (Songkhla LAO survey) + OpenStreetMap waterway length
provenance.methodology: W = 0.5 × (waste density ÷ max over zones) + 0.5 × (OSM waterway line length density ÷ max over zones); ratio-to-max scaling (not min–max) because there are only 4 zones. This zone: 9.112 t/day/km² (allocated); 2.888 km of mapped waterway lines = 0.583 km/km².
limitations: Zone waste density is itself an allocation by population share, so this term mirrors population density.
Proxy for co-location of waste pressure and open channels; it does not measure blockage. Relative within Hat Yai only.

provenance.sourceName: Urban Intelligence illustrative flood-risk / accumulation model v1.0.0
provenance.methodology: Modelled flood-risk score (class low, completeness 1) from computeAreaRisk(model v1.0.0) with the BASELINE scenario (10 mm/h × 2 h, capacity reduction 0, obstruction 0.3, upstream 0.2, η 0.95), design intensity 60 mm/h, inputs E = 0.103, W = 0.585, rainSpatialFactor = 1 (area annual rainfall ÷ mean over the city's areas). See docs/SIMULATION_MODEL.md.
limitations: Illustrative scenario output — not an official flood forecast; weights and capacity are demo assumptions.

notesEn: APPROXIMATE zone polygon (demonstration partition along the railway, Phetkasem, Sriphuwanat and Kanjanavanit roads) — not the official legal boundary.

provenance.sourceName: รายงานวิจัยฉบับสมบูรณ์ ENV6405051S 'การศึกษาแนวทางการสร้างชุมชนขยะเป็นศูนย์ ด้วยการแปลงขยะเป็นพลังงาน' (คณะการจัดการสิ่งแวดล้อม ม.สงขลานครินทร์; ทุน กสว./TSRI ปีงบประมาณ 2564)
provenance.geographicScope: Hat Yai City Municipality (เทศบาลนครหาดใหญ่), municipality-wide
provenance.methodology: Published Hat Yai shares ('ณ เดือน สิงหาคม 2564', 8 categories, integer %, sum 100) mapped to the 6 app categories: organic = food; paper = paper; plastic = plastic; glassMetal = glass + metal; other = rubber/leather + textiles + others; hazardous = 0.0 (not a source category). Largest-remainder rounding to 0.1 (no change: inputs are integers).
limitations: Secondary statement in a research report (the report's step 4 'analyse secondary data from Hat Yai Municipality operations… composition of waste at source'); sampling design, sample size and basis (weight vs volume) are not stated.
Shares are integers (±0.5 percentage-point precision).

Plastic 49% / food 22% is very different from Bangkok (plastic 21.0%, organic 54.1%, BMA FY2565) and PCD national descriptions (organic ≈ 64%); it may reflect waste after organics diversion or a volume basis. Treat as indicative.
Hazardous 0.0 = no hazardous category in the source (e-waste parts are inside 'others'); not a measured zero.
Reference date August 2021 (BE 2564); predates the November 2025 flood.
PMC12247160 (cited for Hat Yai waste quantities) contains no composition table; Bangkok or national shares are NOT substituted.

The 4 community zones (เขต 1–4) are an APPROXIMATE demonstration partition built from OSM roads/railway following the municipality's community map — not official legal boundaries. The municipality polygon itself is an OSM trace tagged 'approximate please verify'.

Zone populations are sums of per-community figures printed in the 2022–2023 boundary announcements (partial: 27/28 communities in เขต 1, 24/25 in เขต 3); the city total is DOPA registration (138,582 at 2025-12-31).

Waste: the latest published Hat Yai values are FY BE 2565 (collected 184.09 t/day, generated 276.72 t/day; Songkhla LAO survey); later years are empty. Zone values are allocations by population share (estimated).
PMC12247160 cites 237.75 t/day of household waste (secondary citation, period and method not stated); it is recorded in the sources but not used as a metric.

Composition is Hat Yai-specific (PSU/TSRI research report ENV6405051S, as of 2021-08 (ณ เดือน สิงหาคม 2564, as stated)): organic 22.0%, plastic 49.0%, paper 12.0%, glass & metal 4.0%, other 13.0% (status derived — 8 published categories mapped to 6). Sampling design and weight/volume basis are not stated; the plastic share is far above Bangkok's, so treat it as indicative. Hazardous 0.0 = no hazardous category in the source. Municipality-wide only; zones carry no own composition.

Rainfall is ERA5 reanalysis: the whole municipality falls within essentially one 0.25° cell (the lattice holds 2 distinct cells), so zones are not distinguished by rainfall; ERA5 annual totals exceed the TMD normal (1,756.0 mm/year at 48569, 1991-2020).
Flood exposure (E) uses proximity to Khlong U-Taphao and mapped OSM waterways only — no spatial extent of the November 2025 flood was available.

Drainage stress and modelled flood risk are illustrative outputs of the demo model (baseline scenario) — not an official forecast. No verifiable Hat Yai street-drainage design intensity (mm/h) was found; the model's default assumption is used.
Earlier floods (2000, 2010) are cited only as manual references without dates and are not listed as events.
